title: Morning Glory Disc Anomaly (MGDA): The Comprehensive Clinical Guide
summary: Morning Glory Disc Anomaly is a rare, unilateral, congenital excavation of the optic nerve head characterized by a funnel-shaped peripapillary configuration. This poster provides a fellowship-level deep dive into its pathophysiology, ocular associations, and management.

sections.title: Definition & Pathophysiology
sections.content: MGDA is a congenital excavation of the optic nerve head, typically unilateral. Pathophysiology involves incomplete closure of the embryonic fissure or a defect in the primitive epithelial papilla. It is associated with a scleral defect allowing the peripapillary retina and pigment epithelium to herniate backward into the subarachnoid space.

sections.title: Key Clinical Features (The 5 Signs)
content: 1. Enlarged, excavated, funnel-shaped optic disc
2. Central glial tuft overlying the disc
3. Annulus of chorioretinal pigmentary disturbance
4. Radial arrangement of retinal vessels
5. Deep peripapillary scleral staphyloma

rows: General scleral thinning, not just peripapillary
Situs inversus of vessels, myopic astigmatism

sections.title: Red Flags: High Risk Associations
content: Transsphenoidal basal encephalocele (high risk of meningitis)
Moebius syndrome or PHACE syndrome
Severe Serous Retinal Detachment (occurs in ~30% of cases)
Risk of intracranial vascular abnormalities (Moyamoya)

content.explanation: F-unnel disc; L-eft or right (unilateral); O-utward vessels; W-hite glial tuft; E-xcavation; R-etinal detachment risk

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup Protocol
content: Step 1: Dilated Fundoscopy & OCT (assess macular schisis/detachment)
Step 2: B-Scan Ultrasound (confirm excavation/staphyloma)
Step 3: MRI Brain/Orbit (Mandatory to rule out encephalocele)
Step 4: MRA (rule out intracranial vascular anomalies)

sections.title: Management Guidelines
content: Observation for stable, asymptomatic eyes.
Refractive management for amblyopia (common in MGDA).
Pars Plana Vitrectomy with ILM peeling + gas tamponade for associated peripapillary detachments.
Multidisciplinary consult: Neurosurgery (if encephalocele present) and Geneticists.

sections.title: Clinical Pearls
content: Visual acuity ranges from 20/20 to hand motions, heavily dependent on foveal involvement.
The vessel pattern is distinct: they exit the periphery of the excavation, not the center.
Always investigate the contralateral eye for subtle disc changes.
Avoid lumbar puncture if basal encephalocele is suspected.
